AI.conclusion: The framework enables reliable identification of unfamiliar cases for deferral to clinicians, supporting safer AI-assisted diagnosis in real-world workflows.

title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
summary: Diffusion transformers (DiTs) achieve state-of-the-art image and video generation, but their multi-step sampling and growing parameter count make inference expensive. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is the natural remedy, yet DiT activations shift across timesteps, prompts, and guidance branches, forcing prior methods to re-fit calibration data for every new checkpoint or modality. We present OrbitQuant, a data-agnostic weight-activation quantizer that bypasses range estimation by quantizing in a normalized, rotated basis. In this basis, a randomized permuted block-Hadamard (RPBH) rotation concentrates each coordinate around one fixed, known marginal regardless of the input, so a single Lloyd-Max codebook serves all timesteps, prompts, and layers of a given input dimension. We extend the same quantizer to weight rows offline, absorbing the rotation into the weights so that it cancels inside each linear layer and only a forward rotation on the activations remains at runtime. The same recipe transfers from image to video with no per-modality tuning. Across FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, Wan 2.1, and CogVideoX, it sets the state of the art for PTQ at several low-bit settings. It also pushes PTQ of image diffusion transformers to W2A4 with usable generation quality.

AI.tldr: OrbitQuant is a data-agnostic weight-activation quantizer for diffusion transformers that uses a normalized, rotated basis (randomized permuted block-Hadamard transform) to eliminate per-timestep/prompt calibration, achieving SOTA PTQ results across image and video DiTs (FLUX.1, Wan 2.1, CogVideoX, etc.) down to W2A4 without per-modality tuning.
AI.motivation: Diffusion transformers (DiTs) suffer from expensive multi-step inference due to growing parameter counts; post-training quantization (PTQ) is needed but existing methods fail because DiT activations shift across timesteps, prompts, and guidance branches, requiring retraining calibration data for each new checkpoint or modality.
AI.method: OrbitQuant applies a randomized permuted block-Hadamard (RPBH) rotation to activations, concentrating each coordinate around a fixed known marginal regardless of input, enabling a single Lloyd-Max codebook across all timesteps/prompts/layers. Weight rows are quantized offline with the rotation absorbed into linear layers so only a forward rotation on activations remains at runtime.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art PTQ results across FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, Wan 2.1, and CogVideoX at several low-bit settings, and pushes image diffusion transformer PTQ down to W2A4 with usable generation quality.
AI.conclusion: OrbitQuant provides a data-agnostic, calibration-free PTQ method for DiTs that generalizes across timesteps, prompts, and modalities (image→video) without per-modality tuning, setting new SOTA for low-bit quantization of diffusion transformers.

title: Interpretation-Oriented Cloud Removal via Observation-Anchored Residual Flow with Geo-Contextual Alignment
summary: Cloud removal (CR) is essential for optical remote sensing, serving as a prerequisite for reliable downstream interpretation, such as semantic segmentation and change detection. However, existing CR approaches often prioritize visual realism while overlooking their impact on subsequent analytical tasks, leading to semantic drift and degraded downstream performance. To address this issue, we propose Geo-Anchored Cloud Removal (GACR), a unified framework that jointly ensures faithful reconstruction and robust interpretability. At its core, GACR incorporates Observation-Anchored Residual Flow (OAR-Flow), which reformulates CR as a physically grounded residual inversion process. By anchoring the generative trajectory to the cloudy observation rather than pure noise, OAR-Flow enables fast, stable, and faithful reconstruction. To further preserve semantic structures critical for downstream interpretation, GACR integrates Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment (GCPA) to constrain the reconstruction within a semantic manifold induced by a Vision Foundation Model (VFM). Consequently, GACR strictly maintains the spatial-semantic integrity of complex landscapes. Extensive experiments across six CR datasets and twelve downstream tasks demonstrate that GACR produces superior reconstruction quality while consistently improving downstream task accuracy. The code is available at https://github.com/wzy6055/GACR.

AI.tldr: GACR is a unified cloud removal framework that combines Observation-Anchored Residual Flow (OAR-Flow) for physically grounded reconstruction and Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment (GCPA) with a Vision Foundation Model to preserve semantic structures, improving both reconstruction quality and downstream task accuracy across six datasets and twelve tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing cloud removal approaches prioritize visual realism but neglect downstream task performance, causing semantic drift and degraded accuracy in applications like semantic segmentation and change detection.
AI.method: GACR integrates two key components: (1) Observation-Anchored Residual Flow (OAR-Flow), which reformulates cloud removal as a physically grounded residual inversion process anchored to the cloudy observation rather than pure noise, and (2) Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment (GCPA), which constrains reconstruction within a semantic manifold induced by a Vision Foundation Model (VFM) to preserve spatial-semantic integrity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across six cloud removal datasets and twelve downstream tasks demonstrate that GACR produces superior reconstruction quality while consistently improving downstream task accuracy.
AI.conclusion: GACR effectively bridges cloud removal and downstream interpretation by jointly ensuring faithful reconstruction and robust interpretability, addressing the semantic drift problem in existing CR approaches.

title: EAGLE-360: Embodied Active Global-to-Local Exploration in 360$^\circ$
summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in standard visual understanding, adapting them for active visual search in 360$^\circ$ panoramic environments exposes fundamental limitations. Specifically, standard MLLMs struggle to effectively model inherent panoramic properties, such as severe polar distortion and continuous cylindrical topologies, which significantly degrades target detection accuracy. Consequently, existing panoramic search methods attempt to compensate by relying heavily on fragmented local viewpoints. Burdened by rigid initialization and a lack of global panoramic priors, these approaches suffer from myopic, inefficient exploration and struggle with robust error recovery when targets are out of view. To overcome these challenges, we propose EAGLE-360, a novel Embodied Active Global-to-Local Exploration framework. Rather than performing exhaustive local searches, EAGLE-360 leverages global priors to establish an initial holistic perspective, iteratively reasoning and progressively narrowing the search space. Architecturally, we adapt RoPE Rolling, a coordinate-shifting positional encoding mechanism, to seamlessly model the continuous topologies of panoramas. To facilitate this paradigm, we construct the large-scale EAGLE-360 dataset, comprising 14,000+ 4K panoramas and 70,000+ rounds of high-quality VQA dialogues. By employing a training pipeline that integrates Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), we effectively elicit complex spatial reasoning and tool-calling capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EAGLE-360 establishes a new state-of-the-art for 360$^\circ$ visual search, achieving nearly an 8-fold increase in accuracy over the base model while significantly enhancing exploration efficiency.

AI.tldr: EAGLE-360 is a novel Embodied Active Global-to-Local Exploration framework for 360° panoramic visual search, which addresses MLLMs' limitations with panoramic properties (polar distortion, cylindrical topology) by leveraging global priors, RoPE Rolling positional encoding, a large-scale dataset (14K+ panoramas, 70K+ VQA dialogues), and SFT+GRPO training, achieving an 8-fold accuracy improvement over baselines.
AI.motivation: Standard MLLMs fail to handle panoramic visual search due to poor modeling of polar distortion and continuous cylindrical topologies, leading to myopic, inefficient exploration and poor error recovery in existing methods.
AI.method: Proposes EAGLE-360 with: (1) a global-to-local exploration paradigm using global priors for initial holistic perspective and iterative narrowing; (2) RoPE Rolling, a coordinate-shifting positional encoding for continuous panoramic topology; (3) a large-scale EAGLE-360 dataset (14K+ 4K panoramas, 70K+ VQA rounds); (4) a training pipeline combining Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
AI.result: Establishes new state-of-the-art for 360° visual search, achieving nearly an 8-fold increase in accuracy over the base model with significantly enhanced exploration efficiency.
AI.conclusion: EAGLE-360 effectively overcomes limitations of standard MLLMs in panoramic settings, validating the global-to-local paradigm and the proposed architectural/training innovations for embodied active visual search.

title: Combating Textual Noise and Redundancy: Entropy-Aware Dense Visual Token Pruning
summary: Visual token pruning is a crucial strategy for accelerating VLMs by compressing redundant image patches, yet existing methods often fail to preserve critical cues under dense instructions and fine-grained queries. In this paper, we investigate this failure and identify two underlying bottlenecks: the widespread dispersion of textual noise that corrupts dense cross-modal scoring, and the feature fragmentation inherent to standard token selection. To address these issues, we propose Entropy-Aware Dense Pruning (EADP), a framework that reformulates pruning as a structured compression problem. EADP first leverages statistical entropy to quantify and filter out textual noise, yielding a robust, fine-grained instruction relevance score. Subsequently, instead of naive Top-K selection, EADP casts token selection as a submodular maximization problem with a spatial prior, explicitly ensuring a holistic and non-redundant visual representation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EADP improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of VLMs, robustly preserving fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets while achieving SoTA performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.

AI.tldr: EADP accelerates VLMs by pruning redundant visual tokens using entropy-based noise filtering and submodular maximization for structured token selection, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy-efficiency trade-offs on multimodal benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing visual token pruning methods fail under dense instructions and fine-grained queries due to two bottlenecks: (1) textual noise corrupting cross-modal scoring, and (2) feature fragmentation from standard Top-K token selection.
AI.method: EADP reformulates pruning as structured compression: (1) uses statistical entropy to quantify and filter textual noise for robust fine-grained instruction relevance scoring; (2) casts token selection as submodular maximization with a spatial prior to ensure holistic, non-redundant visual representation.
AI.result: EADP improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of VLMs, robustly preserves fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: EADP effectively addresses the limitations of prior pruning methods by tackling textual noise and feature fragmentation, providing a more robust and structured approach to visual token compression for VLMs.

title: GeoMix: Descriptor-Free Visual Localization via Global Context and Multi-Detector Training
summary: Descriptor-free visual localization eliminates high-dimensional descriptor storage, preserves scene privacy, and simplifies map maintenance, yet its accuracy still lags far behind descriptor-based pipelines. We identify this gap to insufficient geometric discriminability in geometry-only matching. Without visual appearance, current methods underutilize local geometry cues, lack the global context among keypoints, and overfit to a single keypoint detector. We further observe that descriptor-free matching naturally enables multi-detector training, as heterogeneous keypoints can be optimized in a shared geometry-only space without aligning descriptor spaces. Building on these insights, we propose GeoMix, a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels. Locally, directional and distance-aware embeddings enrich neighborhood aggregation with fine-grained spatial structure. Globally, learnable context nodes aggregate and redistribute scene-wide information via cross-attention to resolve ambiguities beyond local receptive fields. At the training level, Mix-Training exploits this detector-agnostic geometry space to learn representations across multiple keypoint detectors. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night show that GeoMix sets a new state of the art among descriptor-free methods, reducing 75th-percentile rotation error by 89\% and translation error by up to 90\% over the previous best, while generalizing zero-shot to unseen detectors and narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines. Code is available at $\href{https://github.com/YejunZhang/Geomix}{\text{this links}}$.

AI.tldr: GeoMix is a descriptor-free visual localization framework that improves geometric discriminability at local, global, and training levels via directional/distance-aware embeddings, learnable context nodes, and multi-detector Mix-Training, achieving state-of-the-art results among descriptor-free methods and significantly narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines.
AI.motivation: Descriptor-free visual localization eliminates high-dimensional descriptor storage, preserves scene privacy, and simplifies map maintenance, but its accuracy lags behind descriptor-based methods due to insufficient geometric discriminability in geometry-only matching, including underutilization of local geometry cues, lack of global context among keypoints, and overfitting to a single keypoint detector.
AI.method: GeoMix strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels: (1) Locally, directional and distance-aware embeddings enrich neighborhood aggregation with fine-grained spatial structure; (2) Globally, learnable context nodes aggregate and redistribute scene-wide information via cross-attention to resolve ambiguities; (3) At training level, Mix-Training exploits the detector-agnostic geometry space to learn representations across multiple keypoint detectors.
AI.result: On MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night, GeoMix achieves state-of-the-art among descriptor-free methods, reducing 75th-percentile rotation error by 89% and translation error by up to 90% over previous best, while generalizing zero-shot to unseen detectors and narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines.
AI.conclusion: GeoMix demonstrates that descriptor-free visual localization can be significantly improved by enhancing geometric discriminability through multi-level architectural innovations and multi-detector training, effectively narrowing the accuracy gap to descriptor-based approaches.

title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
comment: 15 pages main text, provisionally accepted to ECCV 2026
summary: Models trained via Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) serve as the foundational vision encoders for most modern Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs). Despite their widespread adoption, CLIP models exhibit a critical yet underexplored failure mode: irrelevant text appearing within images confounds visual representations, biasing them toward lexical meaning rather than true visual semantics. This robustness issue, commonly described as a Typographic Attack (TA), exposes a vulnerability that poses a significant risk to safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving. To achieve interpretable and effective robustness against TA, we propose a novel, training-free mechanistic interpretability method. Our method provides sampling-based interpretations of hidden state representations and quantitatively attributes semantic versus lexical focus to individual attention heads. Through probabilistic analysis and circuit mining, we isolate specific Vision Transformer (ViT) components that disproportionately encode lexical information, thereby identifying the mechanistic source of TA. We further show that simple interventions applied directly to the identified circuits, without any additional training, can substantially improve robustness against Typographic Attacks in object classification. These interventions, such as selective adjustment of attention weights, also outperform both supervised and training-free defense methods. Our experiments demonstrate that applying the proposed intervention to the vision encoders of several state-of-the-art LVLMs yields substantial gains in Visual Question Answering accuracy under Typographic Attack interference on RIO-Bench. These results confirm both the efficacy and the generalizability of our mechanistic approach. Code is released at https://github.com/Liu-524/SamplingTAR.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies that CLIP vision encoders are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA)—irrelevant text in images biases representations toward lexical meaning over visual semantics. The authors propose a training-free mechanistic interpretability method that isolates attention heads responsible for encoding lexical information, and applies simple interventions (e.g., attention weight adjustments) to those circuits, significantly improving TA robustness in classification and LVLM-based VQA tasks without retraining.
AI.motivation: CLIP models, widely used as vision encoders in LVLMs, suffer from a critical failure mode where irrelevant text in images (Typographic Attacks) biases visual representations toward lexical meaning, posing risks to safety-critical applications like autonomous driving. Existing defenses are limited, and the mechanistic source of this vulnerability is poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors propose a training-free mechanistic interpretability method that: (1) uses sampling-based interpretations of hidden state representations to attribute semantic vs. lexical focus to individual attention heads; (2) conducts probabilistic analysis and circuit mining to isolate ViT components encoding lexical information; (3) applies simple interventions (e.g., selective adjustment of attention weights) directly to identified circuits without additional training.
AI.result: The proposed intervention outperforms both supervised and training-free defense methods. It also generalizes to LVLMs, yielding substantial gains in VQA accuracy under Typographic Attack interference on RIO-Bench.
AI.conclusion: The mechanistic interpretability approach effectively identifies the source of Typographic Attack vulnerability in CLIP-based vision encoders, and simple, training-free interventions on identified circuits provide robust and generalizable defense, confirming both efficacy and generalizability.

title: Seek to Segment: Active Perception for Panoramic Referring Segmentation
summary: Existing referring segmentation models passively process static images captured from fixed perspectives, limiting their applicability in Embodied AI, where agents must perform active perception in the continuous 360$^\circ$ environments. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel task: Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS). In this setting, an agent is required to adjust its viewing direction ($Δθ, Δφ$) to explore the 360$^\circ$ environment, seeking the object specified by a user instruction for segmentation. To tackle this challenging task, we propose PanoSeeker, a memory-augmented agent for efficient APRS. Rather than relying on heuristic scanning, PanoSeeker integrates a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with EgoSphere, an explicit spatial visual memory. By progressively integrating sequential local observations into a unified 360$^\circ$ representation, EgoSphere enables the agent to plan efficient and non-redundant search trajectories. Once the target is found, the agent performs active viewpoint alignment and outputs the segmentation mask. Furthermore, we curate an expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines for Supervised Fine-Tuning, followed by Reinforcement Learning post-training to explicitly optimize PanoSeeker's exploration efficiency. Extensive experiments on our newly established APRS benchmark demonstrate that PanoSeeker achieves superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.

AI.tldr: PanoSeeker introduces Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS) where an agent actively explores 360° environments to find and segment objects specified by user instructions. It uses a VLM with EgoSphere memory, fine-tuning on expert trajectories, and reinforcement learning to achieve efficient search and accurate segmentation.
AI.motivation: Existing referring segmentation models are passive, processing static images from fixed perspectives, which limits applicability in Embodied AI where agents need active perception in continuous 360° environments.
AI.method: PanoSeeker integrates a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with EgoSphere, an explicit spatial visual memory that progressively unifies local observations into a 360° representation for efficient trajectory planning. It is trained via Supervised Fine-Tuning on expert-annotated data and Reinforcement Learning post-training to optimize exploration efficiency.
AI.result: PanoSeeker achieves superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines on the newly established APRS benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The memory-augmented active perception approach (PanoSeeker) effectively bridges the gap between passive referring segmentation and active embodied perception, enabling non-redundant search trajectories and accurate segmentation in 360° environments.

title: From SRA to Self-Flow: Data Augmentation or Self-Supervision?
summary: Representation alignment has become an effective way to accelerate diffusion transformer training and improve generation quality. Recent self-alignment methods, such as SRA and Self-Flow, further remove the dependency on external pretrained encoders by constructing alignment within the diffusion model itself. However, the mechanism behind the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow, dual-time scheduling, remains under-examined: Self-Flow attributes its gain to interactions between tokens at different noise levels, where cleaner tokens help infer noisier ones. In this work, we revisit this explanation and ask whether the gain instead comes from data augmentation along the noise dimension. To disentangle these factors, we introduce Attention Separation, which preserves the same dual-timestep input as Self-Flow while blocking attention between tokens assigned to different noise levels. Surprisingly, removing such interaction does not degrade performance and can even improve it, suggesting that the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow mainly comes from data augmentation. Furthermore,We show that Attention Separation itself provides an augmentation effect by splitting a single image into multiple effective training parts to expand the training data. Based on these observations, we combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation, and demonstrate the effectiveness of this design on ImageNet.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates whether performance gains from dual-time scheduling in self-alignment diffusion transformers come from cross-token interactions or data augmentation. By introducing Attention Separation (blocking cross-noise-level attention), the authors find augmentation is the key factor, not token interaction, and propose combining self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation.
AI.motivation: To disentangle and understand the true mechanism behind improvements from SRA to Self-Flow (dual-time scheduling) in diffusion transformer self-alignment — specifically whether gains stem from cross-noise-level token interactions or data augmentation along the noise dimension.
AI.method: Introduced Attention Separation, which preserves dual-timestep input like Self-Flow but blocks attention between tokens assigned to different noise levels. Compared performance with and without cross-noise-level attention to isolate the effect of token interaction vs. data augmentation.
AI.result: Removing cross-noise-level token interaction (Attention Separation) does not degrade performance and can even improve it, indicating the main gain of Self-Flow over SRA comes from data augmentation, not token interaction. Attention Separation itself provides augmentation by splitting a single image into multiple effective training parts.
AI.conclusion: The improvement from SRA to Self-Flow is primarily due to data augmentation along the noise dimension, not dual-timestep token interactions. Combining self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation yields effective performance on ImageNet.

title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
summary: State-of-the-art single-image 3D reconstruction methods often rely on complex hybrid architectures and loss functions, or compress geometry into latent spaces in order to leverage pre-trained latent diffusion models. In this work, we show that such architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary. We introduce a minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer, built on a plain ViT, that operates directly on raw 3D point map patches and is conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3. Unlike existing latent diffusion approaches, we train our diffusion backbone entirely from scratch, eliminating the need for point map tokenizers. Despite its simplicity, our approach surpasses complex latent-based diffusion models while remaining significantly simpler than hybrid alternatives. Notably, it produces sharper geometric structure and is more robust in highly ambiguous regions, such as transparent objects.

AI.tldr: A minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer (plain ViT) operating directly on raw 3D point map patches, conditioned on DINOv3 image tokens, outperforms complex latent-based diffusion models and hybrid architectures for single-image 3D reconstruction without needing point map tokenizers or intricate loss functions.
AI.motivation: To show that complex hybrid architectures, latent compression, and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary for single-image 3D reconstruction; a simpler pixel-space Diffusion Transformer can achieve superior results.
AI.method: A pixel-space Diffusion Transformer built on a plain ViT, operating directly on raw 3D point map patches, conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3, trained entirely from scratch without point map tokenizers.
AI.result: Surpasses complex latent-based diffusion models while being significantly simpler than hybrid alternatives; produces sharper geometric structure and is more robust in highly ambiguous regions (e.g., transparent objects).
AI.conclusion: Architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary for state-of-the-art single-image 3D reconstruction; the proposed simple approach is effective and robust.

title: Alignment Is All You Need For X-to-4D Generation
summary: Generative diffusion models excel at synthesizing high-quality images, videos, and 3D content under multimodal control. However, arbitrary user-defined modality-to-4D (X-to-4D) generation remains challenging due to the high cost of constructing diverse datasets and the limited scalability of existing methods. This paper presents Align4D, a flexible framework that translates any-modal input into coherent video-3D pairs, using video to guide 4D motion and 3D data to shape 4D geometry. Align4D introduces three key techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment, which searches Video-Aligned and Multiview-Aligned Object Distances (VAOD/MAOD), respectively, to reconcile 4D renderings with video and the priors of multiview diffusion models; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, which constrains known and unknown views through synchronized video and 3D inputs, ensuring consistent 4D generation; and (3) Asynchronous Optimization, which decouples Gaussian attribute and deformation network training to enhance motion and geometry fidelity. We further propose the X4D dataset, which integrates prompt, image, video, and 3D data for benchmarking. Experiments on X4D and Consistent4D demonstrate that Align4D achieves state-of-the-art quality and consistency in X-to-4D generation. Project page: https://miaoqiaowei.github.io/Align4D/.

AI.tldr: Align4D is a framework for converting any input modality (text, image, video, 3D) into coherent 4D content (video-3D pairs). It uses Object Distance Alignment, Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, and Asynchronous Optimization to achieve state-of-the-art quality and consistency, benchmarked on the proposed X4D dataset.
AI.motivation: Arbitrary user-defined modality-to-4D (X-to-4D) generation is challenging due to high dataset construction costs and limited scalability of existing methods.
AI.method: Three key techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment (VAOD/MAOD) to reconcile 4D renderings with video and multiview diffusion priors; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment for synchronized video and 3D input constraints; (3) Asynchronous Optimization decoupling Gaussian attribute and deformation network training.
AI.result: State-of-the-art quality and consistency on X4D and Consistent4D benchmarks for X-to-4D generation.
AI.conclusion: Align4D provides a flexible, scalable framework for any-modal to 4D generation, achieving superior results over existing methods.

title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
summary: We present WorldDirector, a highly controllable video world model framework designed for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration. Unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, our framework explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. By leveraging an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera movements and subsequently employing these orchestrated trajectories as control signals for video generation, our approach ensures strict physical logic and appearance stability, successfully preserving the exact visual identities of dynamic entities even when they re-enter the scene after prolonged periods out of view. Experimental results demonstrate that our method supports the synthesis of complex and extended events with unprecedented controllability and persistent dynamic object memory. Project Page: https://worlddirector.github.io/

AI.tldr: WorldDirector is a video world model that decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation using an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories and camera movements, enabling persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration with strict physical logic and appearance stability.
AI.motivation: Existing world models entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, failing to preserve visual identities of dynamic entities when they re-enter the scene after prolonged periods out of view.
AI.method: An LLM coordinates 3D trajectories with camera movements, then uses these orchestrated trajectories as control signals for video generation, explicitly decoupling semantic motion orchestration from visual generation.
AI.result: The method supports synthesis of complex and extended events with unprecedented controllability and persistent dynamic object memory.
AI.conclusion: WorldDirector achieves strict physical logic and appearance stability, successfully preserving exact visual identities of dynamic entities even after prolonged occlusion.
